It also identifies clinically transferable features of Dravet syndrome, including fever sensitivity, early seizure onset, and a previously SCN1A-negative Dravet-like presentation caused by a PCDH19 deletion, but finds no vaccination-proximate difference in cognitive decline in Dravet syndrome.
papers.why: Meta-analysis of 271 PCDH19-variant cases provides validated prognostic use of seizure-onset age and characterizes psychiatric and developmental outcome measures in a Dravet-like disorder.

papers.title: The human epilepsy mutation GABRG2(Q390X) causes chronic subunit accumulation and neurodegeneration.
papers.summary: The GABRG2(Q390X) variant produced a severe Dravet syndrome-like phenotype in a knock-in mouse, including spontaneous seizures, mortality, and behavioral comorbidities. Mechanistically, truncated γ2(Q390X) subunits accumulated in the endoplasmic reticulum, impaired inhibitory neurotransmission, increased ER stress and caspase 3 activation, and were associated with age-dependent protein aggregation and neurodegeneration.
papers.why: The knock-in model experimentally links a human GABRG2 epilepsy mutation to receptor aggregation, caspase activation, and neurodegeneration, providing a reusable severe-epilepsy mechanism model.

papers.title: Pitfalls in genetic testing: the story of missed SCN1A mutations.
papers.summary: The study found that many SCN1A mutations in Dravet syndrome were missed by Sanger sequencing, primarily because of human and technical errors, supporting routine second-technique testing after a negative result. Next-generation sequencing detected 28 mutations missed by Sanger sequencing but missed one mutation, while array comparative genomic hybridization detected two SCN1A deletions in patients remaining negative by conventional screening.
papers.why: The study documents technical and human errors causing missed SCN1A variants and supports combining Sanger sequencing with NGS for reliable Dravet diagnosis.

papers.title: Molecular diagnosis of patients with epilepsy and developmental delay using a customized panel of epilepsy genes.
papers.summary: A customized HaloPlex next-generation sequencing panel identified presumed disease-causing variants in 17 of 87 patients with epilepsy and developmental delay, including a novel paternally inherited PCDH19 variant in the only patient classified as having severe myoclonic epilepsy of infancy (Dravet syndrome). The study supports multigene panel testing for severe pediatric epilepsies, while also documenting missed diagnoses caused by genes or variant types outside the panel design.
papers.why: The study reports a targeted NGS diagnostic panel that identified SCN1A and other epilepsy genes in pediatric patients with epilepsy and developmental delay, including early-onset epileptic encephalopathy phenotypes.

papers.title: Autism spectrum disorder and cognitive profile in children with Dravet syndrome: Delineation of a specific phenotype.
papers.summary: In a cohort of 30 children with Dravet syndrome, standardized developmental and autism assessments identified intellectual disability in 77%, autism spectrum disorder in 39%, and social communication disorder in 7%. The study supports early multidomain cognitive assessment and the use of ADI-R, ADOS-2, and parental questionnaires, but found no significant association between autism spectrum disorder and SCN1A mutation, seizure-onset age, or status epilepticus at onset.
papers.why: The study supplies data supporting standardized cognitive, autism, socialization, motor, and adaptive-behavior measures for characterizing Dravet syndrome.

papers.title: Widespread genomic influences on phenotype in Dravet syndrome, a 'monogenic' condition.
papers.summary: In 34 adults with SCN1A-related Dravet syndrome, whole-genome analysis showed that rare variants in additional epilepsy-related genes and genome-wide polygenic variation contribute to phenotypic heterogeneity, including blended molecular diagnoses. Adults with Dravet syndrome had lower intelligence polygenic risk scores and higher longevity polygenic risk scores than epilepsy controls, while a DEPDC5 variant was considered potentially contributory to focal cortical dysplasia in one case but was not experimentally validated.
papers.why: The study provides patient-level evidence that polygenic scores and background rare-variant burden can help explain phenotypic heterogeneity in SCN1A-related Dravet syndrome.

papers.title: Zebrafish studies identify serotonin receptors mediating antiepileptic activity in Dravet syndrome.
papers.summary: In scn1lab mutant zebrafish that recapitulate Dravet syndrome, three novel clemizole analogues and several known serotonin-receptor ligands suppressed convulsive swimming and, for selected compounds, electrographic seizure activity. Receptor-binding and structure–activity data implicate 5-HT2B receptors as a common mediator of seizure suppression, although the precise cellular mechanism remains unresolved.
papers.why: The study tests drug candidates in a Dravet zebrafish model and identifies three antiepileptic clemizole analogues while implicating 5-HT2B as a mechanism of seizure suppression.

papers.title: Cannabidiol improves survival and behavioural co-morbidities of Dravet syndrome in mice.
papers.summary: In two mouse models of Dravet syndrome, chronic cannabidiol increased survival and, in the Scn1a+/− model, improved social interaction, anxiety-like and depression-like behaviour, and spatial memory without improving gait or motor performance. These findings support a potential disease-modifying effect of the studied pharmaceutical formulation of cannabidiol, but the results are preclinical and cannot be directly extrapolated to other cannabidiol formulations or humans.
papers.why: Two Dravet mouse-model experiments show that cannabidiol improves survival, motor and social outcomes, memory, and anxiety- and depression-like behaviours.

papers.title: Delayed maturation of GABAergic signaling in the Scn1a and Scn1b mouse models of Dravet Syndrome.
papers.summary: The study shows that GABAergic signaling matures abnormally slowly in two mouse models of Dravet syndrome: GABA reversal potentials remain depolarized in hippocampal and neocortical pyramidal neurons of Scn1b−/− and Scn1a+/− mice. Acute bumetanide suppresses GABA-evoked firing in Scn1b−/− neurons, while chronic systemic treatment delays SUDEP in a subset of mice but does not prevent seizures or improve failure to thrive.
papers.why: The study directly uses Dravet syndrome mouse models to identify delayed GABAergic maturation and tests bumetanide as an intervention affecting SUDEP risk.

papers.title: Modeling NaV1.1/SCN1A sodium channel mutations in a microcircuit with realistic ion concentration dynamics suggests differential GABAergic mechanisms leading to hyperexcitability in epilepsy and hemiplegic migraine.
papers.summary: A two-neuron conductance-based model and cortical slice experiments indicate that loss-of-function SCN1A/NaV1.1 mutations associated with Dravet syndrome make GABAergic interneurons more susceptible to depolarization block. This suppression of inhibitory interneuron firing produces early pyramidal-neuron hyperexcitability without a necessary increase in GABAergic firing frequency, although the model does not reproduce full seizures or seizure propagation.
papers.why: The computational model directly reproduces mechanistic consequences of epileptogenic SCN1A mutations and can be reused to study network hyperexcitability in Dravet syndrome.

papers.title: Dravet syndrome-associated mutations in GABRA1, GABRB2 and GABRG2 define the genetic landscape of defects of GABAA receptors.
papers.summary: Sequencing of 870 patients with Dravet syndrome identified nine variants in GABRA1, GABRB2, or GABRG2, defining a shared genetic landscape involving the α1β2γ2 GABAA receptor. Cellular functional studies showed predominantly gating defects for selected α1 and β2 variants, whereas GABRG2 T90R caused marked receptor retention and impaired trafficking; GABRB2 F331S had no detectable gating or current-amplitude defect.
papers.why: Large-cohort sequencing and functional receptor assays show distinct gating and trafficking defects among Dravet-associated GABR variants, providing mechanistic and diagnostic biomarkers.

papers.title: Drug repurposing for Dravet syndrome in scn1Lab-/- mutant zebrafish.
papers.summary: In larval scn1Lab−/− zebrafish, efavirenz and lisuride reduced seizure-associated locomotor activity and forebrain epileptiform discharges, whereas rizatriptan was inactive in the Dravet syndrome model. Efavirenz showed the broadest activity across the genetic, pentylenetetrazol, and treatment-resistant ethyl ketopentenoate models, while lisuride was selectively active in the genetic Dravet syndrome model.
papers.why: The study directly tests repurposed marketed drugs in a Dravet syndrome zebrafish model and identifies lisuride as a candidate antiseizure treatment.

papers.title: Time of Day and a Ketogenic Diet Influence Susceptibility to SUDEP in Scn1a R1407X/+ Mice.
papers.summary: In Scn1aR1407X/+ mice modeling Dravet syndrome, spontaneous generalized tonic-clonic seizures and SUDEP were most frequent during the dark phase, and seizure frequency surged during the final 1–2 days before death. A ketogenic diet increased survival to P60 from 44% to 86% and increased circulating β-hydroxybutyrate, but it did not significantly reduce spontaneous seizure frequency or severity, leaving the protective mechanism unresolved.
papers.why: This Dravet syndrome mouse study directly shows ketogenic-diet protection against premature mortality and SUDEP and quantifies seizure and survival outcomes.

papers.title: Fenfluramine: A Review in Dravet and Lennox-Gastaut Syndromes.
papers.summary: This review reports that low-dose adjunctive fenfluramine substantially and durably reduces pharmacoresistant convulsive seizures in patients with Dravet syndrome, with some evidence of improvement in everyday executive functioning but mixed results on broader quality-of-life measures. It also reports decreased appetite and weight loss as common adverse effects, while no valvular heart disease or pulmonary arterial hypertension was observed under protocol-monitored low-dose treatment.
papers.why: Clinical-trial data summarized in the review show durable seizure reductions and possible executive-function benefits from adjunctive fenfluramine in Dravet syndrome.

papers.title: Phenotype-Based Screening of Synthetic Cannabinoids in a Dravet Syndrome Zebrafish Model.
papers.summary: A two-stage phenotype-based screen in homozygous scn1lab zebrafish larvae identified five synthetic cannabinoids that reduced seizure-like swimming and spontaneous electrographic epileptiform events. The findings support larval zebrafish as a screening platform for Dravet syndrome drug discovery, but acute exposure, unknown pharmacokinetics, seizure liability, serious adverse effects, and lack of intended human or veterinary use limit immediate translational application.
papers.why: The study directly screens five synthetic cannabinoids in a Dravet zebrafish model and confirms anticonvuls activity with electrophysiology.

papers.title: An Open Label Extension Study of Cannabidiol (GWP42003-P) in Children and Adults With Dravet or Lennox-Gastaut Syndromes
papers.summary: To investigate the potential antiepileptic effects of cannabidiol (GWP42003-P) in children and adults with Dravet or Lennox-Gastaut syndromes.

papers.title: A Study to Investigate the Transition of Children From 'Artisanal" Cannabidiol (CBD) to Epidiolex
papers.summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn the best way to switch children with Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome (LGS) or Dravet Syndrome (DS) taking 'artisanal' (non pharmaceutical-grade) cannabidiol (CBD) to Epidiolex for treatment of seizures. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How well does a gradual switch from 'artisanal' CBD to Epidiolex work?
* Does the same dose of Epidiolex as 'artisanal' CBD work best?
* What side-effects or medical problems do participants have when switching from 'artisanal' CBD to Epidiolex?

Researchers will examine how successful switching from 'artisanal' CB

papers.title: A Phase 3, Placebo-Controlled Study to Investigate LP352 in Children and Adults With Dravet Syndrome (DS)
papers.summary: This (DEEp SEA Study) is a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, multicenter study to investigate the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of LP352 in the treatment of seizures in children and adults with DS. The study consists of 3 main phases: Screening, Titration period, and Maintenance period, followed by a Taper period and Follow-Up. Participants will be randomized to LP352 or placebo. The total duration of the study will be approximately 24 months.

papers.title: A Phase 2, Multicenter, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Study to Evaluate the Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability of TAK-935 (OV935) as an Adjunctive Therapy in Pediatric Participants With Developmental and/or Epileptic Encephalopathies
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to investigate the effect on the frequency of all seizures (convulsive and drop) in participants treated with TAK-935 compared to placebo.

papers.title: Study to Investigate LP352 in Subjects With Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathies
papers.summary: The objective of this study is to assess the safety, tolerability, efficacy, and pharmacokinetics of adjunctive therapy of LP352 in adults and adolescents with developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.

papers.title: A Study of Soticlestat in Adults and Children With Rare Epilepsies
papers.summary:
The main aim is to assess the long-term safety and tolerability of soticlestat when used along with other anti-seizure treatment.

Participants will receive soticlestat twice a day. Participants will visit the study clinic every 2-6 months throughout the study.

Study treatments may continue as long as the participant is receiving benefit from it.

papers.title: A Clinical Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of ETX101 in Infants and Children With SCN1A-Positive Dravet Syndrome
papers.summary: ENDEAVOR is a Phase 1/2, 2-part, multicenter study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of ETX101 in participants with SCN1A-positive Dravet syndrome aged ≥6 to \<36 months (Part 1A), aged ≥48 months to \<18 years (Part 1B), and aged ≥6 to \<48 months (Part 2). Part 1A follows an open-label, dose-escalation design, Part 1B follows an open-label design, and Part 2 is a randomized, double-blind, sham delayed-treatment control study.

papers.title: A Study to Investigate the Long-Term Safety of ZX008 (Fenfluramine Hydrochloride) Oral Solution in Children and Adults With Epileptic Encephalopathy Including Dravet Syndrome and Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome
papers.summary: This is an international, multicenter, open-label, long-term safety study of ZX008 in subjects with Dravet syndrome, Lennox-Gastaut syndrome or epileptic encephalopathy

papers.title: Bioavailability of Stiripentol After Single Oral Dose of Capsule vs Suspension in Healthy Subjects (STILIQ)
papers.summary:
This is a Phase I, open-label, randomized, single-center, two-way cross-over study evaluating the relative bioavailability, pharmacokinetics, safety, and palatability of two formulations of stiripentol (Diacomit®), indicated in Dravet syndrome. The investigational products are 500 mg capsules (reference) and a 50 mg/mL oral suspension (test).

The primary objective is to compare the relative bioavailability of the two formulations after a single 1,000 mg oral dose under fed conditions, based on Cmax, AUC0-t, and AUC0-∞. Secondary objectives include other PK parameters (tmax, tlag, ke, t1/2) an

papers.title: Open-label, Long-term Safety Study of LP352 in Subjects With Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy
papers.summary: The objective of this study is to assess the long-term safety, tolerability, and efficacy of adjunctive therapy of LP352 in subjects with developmental and epileptic encephalopathies who completed participation in Study LP352-201.

papers.title: A Study of Soticlestat as an Add-on Therapy in Children and Adults With Dravet Syndrome or Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome
papers.summary:
The main aim of the study is to learn if soticlestat, when given as an add-on therapy, reduces the number of seizures in children and adults with Dravet Syndrome (DS) or Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome (LGS).

Participants will receive their standard anti-seizure therapy, plus tablets of soticlestat. There will be scheduled visits and follow-up phone calls throughout the study.

papers.title: Ataluren for Nonsense Mutation in CDKL5 and Dravet Syndrome
papers.summary: This is a phase 2, crossover study of Ataluren for the treatment of nonsense mutation Dravet syndrome or cyclin-dependent kinase-like 5 (CDKL5) deficiency, resulting in drug-resistant epilepsy. Patients will receive 12 weeks of ataluren or placebo during each treatment period. Treatment Period 1 will be followed by a 4-week Washout Period. Based on ataluren PK and pharmacodynamic data, the 4-week washout period is deemed an appropriate length of time to eliminate any ataluren drug effects. Following the Washout Period, patients will crossover to receive the opposite treatment during Treatment

papers.title: A Study to Evaluate Safety, Tolerability, and Pharmacokinetics of Fenfluramine (Hydrochloride) in Infants 1 Year to Less Than 2 Years of Age With Dravet Syndrome
papers.summary: The primary purpose of this study is evaluate the safety and tolerability of fenfluramine hydrochloride (HCl) 0.2 to 0.8 mg/kg/day in infants 1 year to less than 2 years of age with Dravet syndrome.

papers.title: Research on Cognitive Effect of Cannabidiol on Dravet Syndrome and Lennox-Gastaut SyndromeGastaut Syndrome
papers.summary:
The clinical trial "A Prospective Single-Center Single-Arm Clinical Trial on Cognitive Effect of Cannabidiol (CBD-OS®) on Dravet syndrome and Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome" is a single-group phase III study done in single tertiary referral center in Seoul, Korea.

Chief investigator is Dr. Hoon-Chul Kang of Severance Hospital, Yonsei University College of Medicine. Associate investigators are Dr. Heung Dong Kim, Joon Soo Lee, Se Hee Kim, Han Som Choi, Ji Hoon Na, Dong Hwa Yang, and Hee Jung Kang, of Severance Hospital, Yonsei University College of Medicine.

The aim of the study is to evaluate the e

papers.title: Assessment of Adjunctive Cannabidiol Oral Solution (GWP42003-P) in Children With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC), Dravet Syndrome (DS), or Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome (LGS) Who Experience Inadequately-controlled Seizures
papers.summary: This study will be conducted to evaluate the safety, pharmacokinetics (PK), and efficacy of adjunctive GWP42003-P in participants \< 2 years of age with tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC), Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (LGS), or Dravet syndrome (DS).

papers.title: A Trial of Two Fixed Doses of ZX008 (Fenfluramine HCl) in Children and Young Adults With Dravet Syndrome
papers.summary: Study 1 and Study 3 are the prospective, merged analyses of 2 identical double-blind, placebo-controlled studies, ZX008-1501 and ZX008-1502, to assess the efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetics of ZX008 when used as adjunctive therapy in pediatric and young adult subjects with Dravet syndrome. Study 1501 and Study 1502 were conducted in parallel; Study 1501 was conducted at approximately 30 study sites in North America; Study 1502 was conducted at approximately 30 study sites in Europe, Asia and Australia. Upon completion of the Baseline Period after initial Screening and Baseline charting of

papers.title: A Double-blind Study Evaluating the Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability of Zorevunersen in Patients With Dravet Syndrome
papers.summary: The purpose of the study is to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of zorevunersen in Patients with Dravet syndrome.

papers.title: The FINTEPLA as an Anti-SUDEP Therapy in Dravet Syndrome Project
papers.summary: This study investigates cerebrovascular reactivity (CVR) and functional brain connectivity in Dravet Syndrome (DS) patients with convulsive seizures. Using functional MRI (fMRI), we will define differences in brain responses to CO₂ changes before administration of the drug Fintepla (Baseline), with a library of healthy controls and with those obtained after administration of Fintepla (Day \~60). Changes in CVR and their relation to ventilatory responses will also be assessed during fMRI.

papers.title: Antiepileptic Efficacy Study of GWP42003-P in Children and Young Adults With Dravet Syndrome (GWPCARE1)
papers.summary: To investigate the potential antiepileptic effects of cannabidiol (GWP42003-P) in children and young adults with Dravet syndrome.

papers.title: GWPCARE2 A Study to Investigate the Efficacy and Safety of Cannabidiol (GWP42003-P) in Children and Young Adults With Dravet Syndrome
papers.summary: To investigate the potential antiepileptic effects of cannabidiol (GWP42003-P) in children and young adults with Dravet syndrome.

papers.title: A Study to Assess the Safety and Tolerability of ZX008 in Children and Young Adults With Dravet Syndrome or Lennox Gastaut Syndrome Currently Taking Cannabidiol
papers.summary: This is an open label study to evaluate the safety of ZX008 (fenfluramine) in patients with Dravet syndrome (DS) or Lennox Gastaut syndrome (LGS) who are being administered cannabidiol (CBD).

papers.title: Verapamil as Therapy for Children and Young Adults With Dravet Syndrome
papers.summary: This study will assess how well the drug verapamil can improve control of seizures and dysautonomia symptoms in children and young adults diagnosed with Dravet syndrome. The safety of verapamil when given with all concomitant medications will also be assessed.

papers.title: EXploring novEl Molecular Determinants of DRAvet Syndrome Phenotype Heterogeneity
papers.summary: Dravet syndrome is characterized as a developmental encephalopathy resulting from mutations of SCN1A, the gene encoding the alpha subunit of the voltage-gated sodium channel Nav1.1. The syndrome typically presents with drug-resistant epilepsy and varying degrees of cognitive disorders. Current treatment efficacy may be hindered by insufficient knowledge of undiscovered molecular determinants of the disease and its heterogeneous nature. Utilizing induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) derived from skin biopsies, accessibility to patients' brain neurons has enabled successful modeling of various

papers.title: A Study of EPX-100 (Clemizole Hydrochloride) in Participants With Dravet Syndrome
papers.summary: This is a multicenter, Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of clemizole hydrochloride (EPX-100) as adjunctive therapy in children and adult participants with Dravet syndrome (DS).

papers.title: A Study to Assess the Usability of the Embrace Seizure Detection Watch in Children and Young Adults With Dravet Syndrome
papers.summary: This is an exploratory sub-study to ZX008-1503 \[NCT02823145\]. Subjects will be fitted with an Embrace seizure detection watch and seizures detected by the watch will be compared to those entered into an electronic seizure diary.

papers.title: Study of Safety and Pharmacokinetics of Oral Doses of EPX-100 in Healthy Subjects.
papers.summary: This is a placebo-controlled, double-blind, 2-period study in 3 sequential groups of 8 healthy subjects each. The safety and pharmacokinetics of escalating single and multiple oral doses of EPX-100 will be assessed in fasting healthy subjects and following a high-fat meal.

papers.title: Assessment of Potential for Chronic Liver Injury in Participants Treated With Epidiolex (Cannabidiol) Oral Solution
papers.summary: This study will monitor for potential chronic liver injury and liver fibrosis, in participants treated with cannabidiol oral solution.

papers.title: ASCEND: Safety and Tolerability of ION337 for the Treatment of Dravet Syndrome
papers.summary: The primary purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and tolerability of ION337 in participants with Dravet syndrome (DS).

papers.title: Fenfluramine for Adult Dravet Patients
papers.summary:
Full Title: Fenfluramine for the treatment of refractory Epilepsy in Adult Dravet patients

Short Title: Fenfluramine for Adult Dravet patients

Clinical Phase: Phase III

Sample Size: A total of 15 participants will be included in the study.

Study Population: Adult patients (18 years and older) with drug-resistant epilepsy (maintained on their existing medications, with exception of cannabidiol) and genetically confirmed Dravet syndrome will be recruited to participate in the study.

Accrual Period: 12 months Study Design: Open label, non-randomized and uncontrolled add-on trial in adults (1

papers.title: A Clinical Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of ETX101, an AAV9-Delivered Gene Therapy in Children With SCN1A-positive Dravet Syndrome
papers.summary: EXPEDITION is a Phase 1/2 study in the UK to evaluate the safety and efficacy of ETX101 in participants with SCN1A-positive Dravet Syndrome aged 6 to \< 48 months. The study follows and open-label, dose-escalation design.

papers.title: A Dose-ranging Pharmacokinetics and Safety Study of GWP42003-P in Children With Dravet Syndrome (GWPCARE1)
papers.summary: To evaluate the safety and pharmacokinetics (PK) of multiple doses of GWP42003-P compared with placebo in children with Dravet syndrome.

papers.title: A Study to Evaluate the Safety and Pharmacokinetics of RC001 in Children With Dravet Syndrome
papers.summary: This is an open-label, single-center study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and preliminary efficacy of intrathecal RC001 in patients with Dravet syndrome aged 2 to 18 years. The study includes a dose-escalation part followed by a fixed dose treatment part, with participant progression based on investigator-assessed safety and efficacy.

papers.title: Clobazam as Adjunctive Therapy in Paediatric Patients Aged ≥1 to ≤16 Years With Dravet Syndrome
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to investigate the effect on the frequency of tonic-clonic and clonic seizures of clobazam as adjunctive therapy compared to placebo after 16 weeks of treatment in paediatric patients aged ≥1 to ≤16 years with Dravet Syndrome.

papers.title: Clinical Utility of Reduced EEG Home Monitoring in Fenfluramine Titration for Dravet and LGS
papers.summary:
The goal of this real world data study is to evaluate the clinical utility of remote patient monitoring solution (using Byteflies' EpiCare@Home with reduced EEG montage and other vital signs) with Dravet and LGS patients (ages 3 and up with the exclusion of adults above weight allowing variable titration) to identify an optimal Fenfluramine treatment.

Patients will wear one or more small portable and medically certified measuring devices. Through these devices, electroencephalography (EEG) signals, as well as electro-cardiography (ECG), heart rate, respiration rate, and physical activity are

papers.title: Safety and Tolerability of Clobazam as Adjunctive Therapy in Paediatric Patients Aged ≥1 to ≤16 Years With Dravet Syndrome
papers.summary: To investigate the long-term safety and tolerability of clobazam when administered for 1 year as adjunctive therapy in paediatric patients aged ≥1 to ≤16 years with Dravet Syndrome.

papers.title: An Open-Label Extension Study of STK-001 for Patients With Dravet Syndrome
papers.summary: Stoke Therapeutics is evaluating the long-term safety \& tolerability of repeated doses of zorevunersen (STK-001) in patients with Dravet syndrome who previously participated in studies of zorevunersen. Change in seizure frequency and overall clinical status, and quality of life will be measured as secondary endpoints in this open-label study.

papers.title: A Study of Soticlestat as an Add-on Therapy in Children and Young Adults With Dravet Syndrome
papers.summary:
The main aim of the study is to learn if soticlestat, when given as an add-on therapy, reduces the number of convulsive seizures in children and young adults with DS.

Participants will receive their standard antiseizure therapy, plus either a tablet of soticlestat or placebo for 16 weeks. A placebo looks just like soticlestat but will not have any medicine in it.

Participants may continue treatment in an extension study, based on the extension study's entry criteria. Those that want to stop treatment will have a gradual dose reduction during 1 week and then be followed up for 2 weeks.

papers.title: An Open-Label Extension Trial to Assess the Long-Term Safety of ZX008 (Fenfluramine Hydrochloride HCl) Oral Solution in Children and Young Adults With Dravet Syndrome
papers.summary: This is an international, multicenter, open-label, long-term safety study of ZX008 in subjects with Dravet syndrome.

papers.title: A Study Evaluating Soticlestat in Participants With Dravet Syndrome or Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome Who Have Been Exposed to Fenfluramine
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to check how soticlestat impacts symptoms of Dravet syndrome \[DS\] and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome \[LGS\] in participants who have been exposed to fenfluramine.

papers.title: Cannabidiol Oral Solution as an Adjunctive Therapy for Treatment of Participants With Inadequately Controlled Dravet Syndrome
papers.summary:
This Phase 3 study will enroll participants diagnosed with Dravet Syndrome (DS) who are still experiencing at least one tonic-clonic, clonic, and/or focal seizures with motor components (FSMC) per week, despite ongoing treatment with up to three antiepileptic drugs (AEDs), and meet the other inclusion/exclusion criteria.

Following a 28-day baseline period, participants will begin an 84-day treatment period. Participants will be assigned to receive twice-daily doses of placebo or cannabidiol oral solution at the highest dose determined to be safe in a previous trial.

Following study completio

papers.title: The Effects of Cannabidiol (CBD) on Electrical and Autonomic Cardiac Function in Children With Severe Epilepsy
papers.summary: The investigators propose to study the effects of cannabidiol (CBD) on cardiac electrical function and the autonomic nervous system in children with Dravet syndrome (DS) and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (LGS), when the CBD is administered as an artisanal oil obtained through state dispensaries or other sources. The intent is to begin to assess potential risks and benefits of this therapy in a vulnerable patient population by characterizing the effects of CBD on EKG findings, heart rate variability and the occurrence of seizures.

papers.title: Turmeric as Treatment in Epilepsy
papers.summary: This is a single center open-label pilot clinical trial of patients 1-70 years of age with greater than 6 seizures per month diagnosed with Dravet Syndrome, Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome, Tuberous Sclerosis, or focal seizures. Twenty patients will be enrolled and treated with a stable dose of orally administered turmeric oil daily for 3 months. Patients and caregivers will be asked to keep a seizure diary logging all clinical events during the course of the study. Serum comprehensive metabolic panel, complete blood count with differential, and antiseizure medication levels, will be monitored at base

papers.title: A 2-Part Study to Investigate the Dose-Ranging Safety and Pharmacokinetics, Followed by the Efficacy and Safety of ZX008 (Fenfluramine Hydrochloride) Oral Solution as an Adjunctive Therapy in Children ≥ 2 Years Old and Young Adults With Dravet Syndrome
papers.summary: The primary purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of ZX008 (fenfluramine hydrochloride) when added to adjunctive antiepileptic stiripentol treatment in children and young adults with Dravet syndrome.

papers.title: BMB-101 in Absence Epilepsy and DEE
papers.summary: The study is a pilot, open-label, study to test whether BMB-101 is safe and effective in reducing the frequency of seizures in subjects with Absence Epilepsy including Epilepsy with Eyelid Myoclonia (also called Jeavons Syndrome) as well as Developmental Epileptic Encephalopathies such as Dravet and Lennox Gastaut. The study will last up to 6 months. There will be a 1 month screening period, then up to 3 months on open-label BMB-101 including titration and tapering/washout periods, and then a 1 month follow-up period. There will be 6 clinic visits.

papers.title: CBD Delivery with the A-Synaptic GT4 Transdermal Delivery System in with Dravet Syndrome And/or Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome
papers.summary:
This study is a preliminary open-label, single-arm Phase II investigation into the safety and efficacy of transdermal cannabidiol (CBD) delivered using GT4 skin bream technology in individuals diagnosed with Dravet and/or Lennox-Gastatu syndrome (DS and/or LGS). We aim to enroll 25 participants between the ages of 2 and 55 diagnosed with DS and/or LGS.

Transdermal delivery of cannabinoids may provide advantages over other traditional routes of administration. Noted advantages include avoidance of first pass metabolism which mitigates potentially dangerous drug-drug interactions due to delayed

papers.title: A Study of Lorcaserin as Adjunctive Treatment in Participants With Dravet Syndrome
papers.summary: The primary purpose of the study is to demonstrate that lorcaserin has superior efficacy compared to placebo on percent change in frequency of convulsive seizures per 28 days in participants with Dravet syndrome.

papers.title: An Open-Label Study to Investigate the Safety of Single and Multiple Ascending Doses in Children and Adolescents With Dravet Syndrome
papers.summary: Stoke Therapeutics is evaluating the safety and tolerability of single and multiple ascending doses of STK-001 in patients with Dravet syndrome. Change in seizure frequency, overall clinical status, and quality of life will be measured as secondary endpoints in this open-label study.

papers.title: Open Targets drug and clinical candidates for Dravet syndrome
Open Targets drugs acting on SCN1A
Open Targets drugs acting on CYP46A1
Open Targets drugs acting on GABRA1
Open Targets drugs acting on GABRG2
Open Targets drugs acting on SCN2A
Genotype-function-phenotype correlations for SCN1A variants identified by clinical genetic testing.
papers.summary: The paper links complete SCN1A loss of function to early-onset febrile seizures and severe, heterogeneous SCN1A-associated epilepsy, including Dravet syndrome, and shows that automated patch-clamp recording plus PV+ interneuron simulation can resolve variant pathogenicity and predict neuronal dysfunction. Clinical follow-up found individualized antiseizure-medication responses, including seizure control with valproic acid in some patients, but no universally effective regimen.

papers.title: Long-read sequencing and profiling of RNA-binding proteins reveals the pathogenic mechanism of aberrant splicing of an  SCN1A  poison exon in epilepsy
papers.summary: The study shows that variants in or near the SCN1A 20N poison exon increase poison-exon inclusion and reduce Na v 1.1 protein abundance, supporting SCN1A haploinsufficiency in SCN1A-related epilepsy. Using patient-derived neuronal iPSCs, splicing assays, long-read and short-read sequencing, western blotting, and RNA-antisense purification, the authors identified 28 RNA-binding proteins with altered variant-construct interactions, including SRSF1 and HNRNPL, and proposed a model in which these proteins regulate aberrant 20N splicing.

papers.title: Development of a high-throughput fluorescent no-wash sodium influx assay.
papers.summary: The paper develops a high-throughput, no-wash fluorescent sodium-influx assay using Asante NaTRIUM Green-2 and Ponceau 4R to measure human NaV1.1–1.8 activity in heterologous cells. For the SCN1A-relevant NaV1.1 mechanism, veratridine activated the channel-associated sodium signal, tetracaine inhibited it, and Ponceau 4R did not measurably alter NaV1.1 pharmacology or electrophysiology.

papers.title: Reduction of Kcnt1 is therapeutic in mouse models of SCN1A and SCN8A epilepsy.
papers.summary: In mouse models carrying Scn1a haploinsufficiency or the gain-of-function Scn8a p.R1872W mutation, a Kcnt1 antisense oligonucleotide reduced Kcnt1 expression and prolonged survival, with incomplete long-term protection in Scn1a+/− mice. Quinidine failed to extend survival in the Scn8a model, while the proposed KCNT1-dependent enhancement of parvalbumin-interneuron excitability remains a hypothesis requiring further investigation.

papers.title: T76. INVESTIGATION OF NAV1.1 POSITIVE MODULATOR EFFECTS ON FAST SPIKING INTERNEURONS IN SOMATOSENSORY CORTEX SLICES
papers.summary: This abstract reports that the selective Nav 1.1 positive modulator Compound 3a increased action-potential-related activity in fast-spiking parvalbumin-positive interneurons from mouse somatosensory cortex slices only under particular recording conditions. The findings suggest that physiological temperature and appropriate ionic composition are important for detecting the electrophysiological effect, but the study does not demonstrate improvement of schizophrenia or transfer to Dravet syndrome.

papers.title: Pharmacology of the Nav1.1 domain IV voltage sensor reveals coupling between inactivation gating processes.
papers.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
papers.summary: The study shows that Hm1a and ICA-121431 differentially modulate the domain IV voltage sensor (VSDIV) of the Na v 1.1 voltage-gated sodium channel and thereby alter fast and slow inactivation. Hm1a inhibits VSDIV movement, increases channel availability during high-frequency stimulation, and hinders both inactivation components, whereas ICA-121431 promotes use-dependent block by accelerating entry into the slow inactivated state.

papers.title: Precisely controlling endogenous protein dosage in hPSCs and derivatives to model FOXG1 syndrome.
papers.summary: The paper applies the SMASh protein-dosage-control system to human pluripotent stem cells and derived neural models to model FOXG1 syndrome. Reducing FOXG1 dosage impairs medial ganglionic eminence progenitor development, GABAergic interneuron induction, maturation, and organoid growth, with severe defects at approximately 30% or less FOXG1 protein.

papers.title: Human Stem Cell-Derived GABAergic Interneurons Establish Efferent Synapses onto Host Neurons in Rat Epileptic Hippocampus and Inhibit Spontaneous Recurrent Seizures.
papers.summary: In immunodeficient rats with kainic acid-induced temporal lobe epilepsy, transplanted human embryonic stem cell-derived GABAergic interneurons matured in the epileptic hippocampus, formed functional inhibitory synapses onto host neurons, and reduced seizure-related activity. Optogenetic activation reduced induced epileptiform discharges in hippocampal slices, while transplantation reduced motor spontaneously recurring seizure frequency and total seizure time in vivo without changing individual seizure duration or severity.

papers.title: Ursolic Acid Protects Neurons in Temporal Lobe Epilepsy and Cognitive Impairment by Repressing Inflammation and Oxidation.
papers.summary: In lithium-pilocarpine-induced temporal lobe epilepsy rats, ursolic acid reduced seizure susceptibility, hippocampal inflammation and oxidative injury, and protected hippocampal neurons and cognitive function. It also attenuated status epilepticus-associated loss of GABAergic interneuron markers, although the 100 mg/kg/day dose often failed to provide neuroprotection or spatial-learning benefit.

papers.title: Arx expansion mutation perturbs cortical development by augmenting apoptosis without activating innate immunity in a mouse model of X-linked infantile spasms syndrome.
papers.summary: In the Arx(GCG)10+7 mouse model of X-linked infantile spasms syndrome, early 17β-estradiol increased cortical Arx-positive GABAergic interneuron density and previously reduced seizures, but it did not reduce the transient increase in cortical apoptosis. ACTH(1-24) also increased Arx-positive interneuron density in motor cortex but lacked convincing spasm or seizure efficacy and did not show that apoptosis mediated the hormone effects.

papers.title: Ablation of Unilateral Hippocampal GABAergic Neurons: A Novel Mouse Model of Mesial Temporal Lobe Epilepsy With Hippocampal Sclerosis.
papers.summary: Selective unilateral ablation of hippocampal GABAergic interneurons in VGAT-Cre mice produced chronic spontaneous recurrent seizures with hippocampal sclerosis, anxiety-like behavior, and cognitive impairment, demonstrating that loss of this mechanism can drive an MTLE-HS phenotype. The model provides a target-specific platform for studying GABAergic interneuron biology and testing therapies, while a cited human MGE-derived GABAergic interneuron cell therapy offers a directly relevant transfer candidate but was not evaluated in this study.

papers.title: GABA acts as a ligand chaperone in the early secretory pathway to promote cell surface expression of GABAA receptors.
papers.summary: In transfected HEK 293 cells, GABA acted as a ligand chaperone that increased surface expression and function of α1β2γ2 gamma-aminobutyric acid type A receptors, including rescue of a receptor construct retained in the secretory pathway. The effects required GABA uptake and early secretory-pathway trafficking, and were blocked by disruption of the receptor's GABA-binding site.

papers.title: Hsp47 Promotes Biogenesis of Multi-subunit Neuroreceptors in the Endoplasmic Reticulum
papers.summary: The paper reports that the endoplasmic-reticulum chaperone Hsp47, encoded by SERPINH1, promotes the assembly and anterograde trafficking of gamma-aminobutyric acid type A receptors, thereby increasing their functional surface expression. Hsp47 acts after BiP, preferentially binds a folded receptor conformation, and has broader effects on other multi-subunit Cys-loop neuroreceptors, including nicotinic acetylcholine receptors.

papers.title: Targeted knockout of GABA-A receptor gamma 2 subunit provokes transient light-induced reflex seizures in zebrafish larvae.
papers.summary: A homozygous gabrg2-knockout zebrafish model, designated R23X, develops transient light- or dark-triggered motor and neuronal hyperexcitability during 3–6 days post-fertilization. Acute valproic acid exposure rescues both phenotypes, supporting their seizure-like nature and suggesting the model is suitable for GABA-A receptor-related epilepsy and drug screening.

papers.title: The neuroplastin adhesion molecules are accessory proteins that chaperone the monocarboxylate transporter MCT2 to the neuronal cell surface.
papers.summary: The study provides experimental evidence that neuroplastin np55 and np65 bind to MCT2, increase its cell-surface localization, and support lactate transport in COS-7 cells and Xenopus oocytes. It also reports cerebellar co-enrichment of neuroplastin and MCT2, but contains no experimental intervention on the alpha-1 beta-2 gamma-2 gamma-aminobutyric acid type A receptor and therefore offers no direct receptor-selective transfer solution for Dravet syndrome.

papers.title: Neurosteroids and Seizure Activity.
papers.summary: This review reports that neurosteroids can positively or negatively modulate GABA-A receptors, with positive modulators generally showing anticonvulsant activity across seizure models and limited clinical populations. Ganaxolone, allopregnanolone, and progesterone reduced seizures in selected patients, but effects were age-, model-, region-, and seizure-type-dependent, and the paper does not establish activity at the alpha-1 beta-2 gamma-2 gamma-aminobutyric acid type A receptor specifically.

papers.title: Experimental GABA A Receptor Agonists and Allosteric Modulators for the Treatment of Focal Epilepsy.
papers.summary: This review identifies GABA A receptor agonists and positive allosteric modulators with reported anticonvulsant activity in focal epilepsy or related animal models. The most transferable candidates for the requested receptor mechanism are α2/α3-subunit-selective modulators, particularly AZD7325, which increased the seizure threshold in Scn1a+/− mice, although the paper does not test the exact alpha-1 beta-2 gamma-2 gamma-aminobutyric acid type A receptor.

papers.title: A phase 3, randomized clinical trial of soticlestat as adjunctive therapy for Lennox-Gastaut syndrome.
papers.summary: The phase 3 SKYWAY trial found that adjunctive soticlestat, a selective inhibitor of CYP46A1/cholesterol 24-hydroxylase, did not reduce major motor drop seizures more than placebo in participants with Lennox–Gastaut syndrome despite an approximately 80% reduction in plasma 24S-hydroxycholesterol. These data do not support transferring soticlestat to Dravet syndrome, although the paper cites a previous mixed LGS/Dravet phase 2 study that reported reduced median seizure frequency; that earlier result is not presented separately for Dravet syndrome.

papers.title: 24S-hydroxycholesterol and 25-hydroxycholesterol differentially impact hippocampal neuronal survival following oxygen-glucose deprivation.
papers.summary: In primary hippocampal neuron cultures, CYP46A1-dependent production of 24S-hydroxycholesterol increased oxygen-glucose deprivation-induced, NMDAR-dependent neuronal death, whereas reducing endogenous 24S-HC synthesis was protective. The oxysterol 25-HC partially reversed 24S-HC-exacerbated toxicity and showed modest, species-dependent NMDAR-independent neuroprotection in rat but not mouse cultures.

papers.title: Anticonvulsive properties of soticlestat, a novel cholesterol 24-hydroxylase inhibitor.
papers.summary: Soticlestat, a small-molecule inhibitor of CYP46A1/CH24H, lowered brain 24S-hydroxycholesterol and reduced seizure development in audiogenic seizure and pentylenetetrazol kindling models. It was ineffective in acutely induced maximal electroshock, scPTZ, and 6-Hz seizures and did not suppress fully established corneal-kindled seizures, suggesting activity during seizure progression and secondary generalization rather than established acute seizures.

papers.title: 27-Hydroxycholesterol Promotes the Transfer of Astrocyte-Derived Cholesterol to Neurons in Co-cultured SH-SY5Y Cells and C6 Cells.
papers.summary: In co-cultured rat C6 astrocyte-like cells and human SH-SY5Y neuronal cells, 27-hydroxycholesterol promoted ApoE-associated cholesterol transfer from C6 cells to SH-SY5Y cells and increased neuronal plasma-membrane cholesterol, Aβ protein, and production of 24S-hydroxycholesterol. The increased 24S-hydroxycholesterol occurred without increased total CYP46A1 expression and was associated with CYP46A1 redistribution from the endoplasmic reticulum to the plasma membrane, supporting a substrate-associated feedback mechanism for cholesterol clearance.

papers.title: Low-Dose Anti-HIV Drug Efavirenz Mitigates Retinal Vascular Lesions in a Mouse Model of Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.summary: In 5XFAD mice with retinal vascular lesions, low-dose efavirenz increased retinal CYP46A1 activity and cholesterol turnover and reduced lesion frequency, vascular leakage, deposits, lipid accumulation, and macrophage/microglia activation. These mouse findings support further investigation of efavirenz as a CYP46A1-activating therapy, but efficacy in neovascular age-related macular degeneration or Dravet syndrome remains unestablished.

papers.title: Role of cholesterol in modulating brain hyperexcitability.
papers.summary: This review identifies CYP46A1 (CH24H)-mediated cholesterol 24-hydroxylation as a mechanism that can promote neuronal hyperexcitability through 24S-hydroxycholesterol, NMDA-receptor potentiation, neuroinflammation, and impaired EAAT2-mediated glutamate clearance. The CYP46A1 inhibitor soticlestat reduced seizures and improved survival in animal models, including an SCN1A-haploinsufficiency model of Dravet syndrome, but whether it provides disease-modifying rather than antiseizure effects remains uncertain.

papers.title: Evaluating bexicaserin for the treatment of developmental epileptic encephalopathies.
papers.summary: This review identifies the serotonergic system as a therapeutic target for developmental epileptic encephalopathies and evaluates bexicaserin, a selective 5-HT2C receptor agonist, as an adjunctive antiseizure medication. It reports reduced motor seizures in clinical studies and activity across seizure models, while noting adverse effects, treatment discontinuation, unresolved mechanism, and uncertain antiepileptogenic potential.

papers.title: Use of fenfluramine in MECP2-related Rett syndrome: Findings from a retrospective multicenter pediatric case series.
papers.summary: In a retrospective series of four children with MECP2-related Rett syndrome and drug-resistant epilepsy, fenfluramine reduced seizure frequency in three patients, including >50% reductions in two, while one patient discontinued treatment without improvement. Caregivers also reported improved alertness, interaction, and irritability, but transient apathy and psychomotor slowing occurred; the small uncontrolled series does not establish efficacy or safety.

papers.title: Deficits in LTP induction by 5-HT2A receptor antagonist in a mouse model for fragile X syndrome.
papers.summary: In a mouse model of fragile X syndrome, serotonin type 2A receptor antagonists R-96544 and ketanserin enhanced long-term potentiation in wild-type anterior cingulate cortex slices but failed to do so in Fmr1 knock-out slices. R-96544 also increased GluR1 surface expression in wild-type cultured prefrontal cortex neurons, whereas this response was absent in Fmr1 knock-out neurons, indicating that FMRP is required for serotonergic modulation of glutamatergic synaptic plasticity.

papers.title: Glial expression of Drosophila UBE3A causes spontaneous seizures that can be modulated by 5-HT signaling.
papers.summary: In a Drosophila Dup15q syndrome model, glial dube3a overexpression produced heat-evoked and spontaneous seizure-associated behavior with centrally generated synchronized spike bursts, whereas neuronal overexpression produced little or no spontaneous bursting. Feeding the serotonergic drugs vortioxetine and ketanserin reduced immobilization and spike bursting, supporting serotonergic modulation as a suppressive mechanism, although neither drug completely reversed hyperexcitability.

papers.title: Autism spectrum disorder-like behaviors induced by hyper-glutamatergic NMDA receptor signaling through hypo-serotonergic 5-HT1A receptor signaling in the prefrontal cortex in mice exposed to prenatal valproic acid.
papers.summary: In male mice exposed to valproic acid prenatally, reduced serotonergic function in the prefrontal cortex was associated with hyper-glutamatergic signaling and autism spectrum disorder-like behavioral abnormalities. Fluoxetine and serotonergic-neuron activation improved social and cognitive phenotypes but not repetitive grooming, whereas the 5-HT1A receptor agonist tandospirone improved all three behavioral categories and reduced CaMKII phosphorylation.

papers.title: Modulatory Effect of Serotonergic System in Pentylenetetrazole-Induced Seizures and Associated Memory Deficit: Role of 5-HT1A and 5-HT2A/2C.
papers.summary: In pentylenetetrazole-kindled mice, the 5-HT2A receptor agonist R (-) DOI reduced seizure severity and improved memory measures, while its anticonvulsant effect was antagonized by the 5-HT2A/2C receptor antagonist olanzapine. The 5-HT1A agonist 8-OH-DPAT improved memory without improving seizure severity, whereas WAY-100,635 reduced seizure severity but was associated with impaired memory, indicating receptor-specific and outcome-specific modulation of the serotonergic system.

unread.title: GABRA1 and STXBP1: novel genetic causes of Dravet syndrome.
unread.why: The study identifies disease-causing GABRA1 and STXBP1 variants in SCN1A-negative Dravet syndrome and demonstrates a sequencing approach with diagnostic implications.

unread.title: Spectrum of SCN1A gene mutations associated with Dravet syndrome: analysis of 333 patients.
unread.why: Analysis of 333 Dravet syndrome patients provides a validated sequencing and MLPA strategy for detecting point mutations, deletions, and other SCN1A rearrangements.

unread.title: A functional null mutation of SCN1B in a patient with Dravet syndrome.
unread.why: The paper directly models a Dravet-associated SCN1B loss-of-function mechanism using biochemical assays and knockout mice with electrophysiological seizure phenotyping.

unread.title: Gabra2 is a genetic modifier of Dravet syndrome in mice.
unread.why: Repairing Gabra2 in a Scn1a+/- mouse model restored receptor expression and rescued epilepsy phenotypes, supporting a genetically validated therapeutic target for Dravet syndrome.

unread.title: Channelopathy of Dravet Syndrome and Potential Neuroprotective Effects of Cannabidiol.
unread.why: Although it is a review, it synthesizes human and animal evidence for cannabidiol and identifies the ion-channel mechanisms through which it may treat Dravet syndrome.

unread.title: State-of-the-art management of Dravet syndrome.
unread.why: The review summarizes randomized-trial and real-world evidence for established Dravet therapies, natural-history outcomes, and emerging precision disease-modifying approaches.

unread.title: Engineering a human-based translational activator for targeted protein expression restoration.
unread.why: The study demonstrates in a Dravet mouse model that engineered CIRTS-4GT3 increases SCN1a translation and improves survival and seizure threshold, providing a reusable gene-therapy method.

unread.title: The GABRG2 nonsense mutation, Q40X, associated with Dravet syndrome activated NMD and generated a truncated subunit that was partially rescued by aminoglycoside-induced stop codon read-through.
unread.why: The study demonstrates that gentamicin partially restores full-length GABRG2 and functional GABA-A receptors in cells carrying a Dravet-associated nonsense mutation, suggesting a concrete rescue strategy.

unread.title: Overexpressing wild-type γ2 subunits rescued the seizure phenotype in Gabrg2<sup>+/Q390X</sup> Dravet syndrome mice.
unread.why: BAC-driven overexpression of wild-type GABRG2 improved receptor function, inhibition, seizure threshold, and network physiology in a Dravet-associated mouse model, providing direct gene-replacement evidence.

unread.title: Sleep slow-wave oscillations trigger seizures in a genetic epilepsy model of Dravet syndrome.
unread.why: The study provides a genetic Dravet-like epilepsy model and experimentally demonstrates optogenetic and pharmacological approaches that trigger or suppress epileptic activity.

unread.title: Modulating Endoplasmic Reticulum Chaperones and Mutant Protein Degradation in GABRG2(Q390X) Associated with Genetic Epilepsy with Febrile Seizures Plus and Dravet Syndrome.
unread.why: The study directly identifies HRD1/ERAD modulation and zonisamide as tested approaches that reduce mutant GABRG2 accumulation, improve receptor trafficking, and reduce seizures in a Dravet-associated model.

unread.title: A screening test for the prediction of Dravet syndrome before one year of age.
unread.why: The study develops and validates a simple clinical screening score that identifies infants at high risk for Dravet syndrome and recommends SCN1A testing at a defined cutoff.

unread.title: Lamotrigine can be beneficial in patients with Dravet syndrome.
unread.why: The report provides patient-level evidence that lamotrigine can reduce seizure frequency and duration in a subset of people with Dravet syndrome.

unread.title: Dravet syndrome: new potential genetic modifiers, imaging abnormalities, and ictal findings.
unread.why: The study identifies clinically useful genetic and electrophysiologic/imaging findings that can refine Dravet syndrome assessment, prognosis, and seizure characterization.

unread.title: The endocannabinoid system impacts seizures in a mouse model of Dravet syndrome.
unread.why: In a Scn1a+/- Dravet mouse model, pharmacologic enhancement of endocannabinoid signaling reduced hyperthermia-induced seizures, providing tested drug candidates and a disease-relevant model.

unread.title: A single-center, retrospective analysis of genotype-phenotype correlations in children with Dravet syndrome.
unread.why: A 137-patient Dravet cohort provides clinically observed genotype-phenotype and medication-response data, including response to the recommended treatment triad, that can guide research and trial design.

unread.title: A review of the putative antiseizure and antiepileptogenic mechanisms of action for soticlestat.
unread.why: The review summarizes completed Dravet phase III studies of soticlestat and mechanistic evidence for its seizure-threshold and neuroinflammatory effects.

unread.title: SCN1A Gene Mutation and Adaptive Functioning in 18 Vietnamese Children with Dravet Syndrome.
unread.why: This Dravet cohort applies the Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales and links adaptive-function outcomes with SCN1A variants and seizure history, providing usable outcome measures.

unread.title: Ataxia and cerebellar hypoexcitability in a mouse model of SCN1B-linked Dravet syndrome.
unread.why: The Scn1b-null model reproduces Dravet-associated ataxia and severe seizures and provides a system for studying cerebellar excitability and seizure mechanisms.

unread.title: Mapping genetic modifiers of survival in a mouse model of Dravet syndrome.
unread.why: The study establishes strain-dependent Scn1a+/- Dravet models and identifies modifier loci and candidate genes, offering a platform for mechanism discovery and treatment development.

unread.title: Successful use of fenfluramine as an add-on treatment for Dravet syndrome.
unread.why: A long-term observational series reports substantial seizure control, including seizure freedom, with fenfluramine in genetically confirmed Dravet syndrome.

unread.title: Development and Validation of a Prediction Model for Early Diagnosis of SCN1A-Related Epilepsies.
unread.why: The multicenter study developed and independently validated an objective model that distinguishes Dravet syndrome from GEFS+ using SCN1A genotype and seizure onset.

unread.title: Stiripentol: A Review in Dravet Syndrome.
unread.why: The review summarizes randomized, observational, and long-term evidence supporting stiripentol as an effective adjunctive treatment for Dravet syndrome.

unread.title: Changing Landscape of Dravet Syndrome Management: An Overview.
unread.why: The review consolidates established and investigational Dravet treatments, including approved drugs, dietary and neuromodulatory therapies, gene-targeted approaches, and seizure-detection devices.

unread.title: Lorcaserin for Dravet Syndrome: A Potential Advance Over Fenfluramine?
unread.why: The article documents lorcaserin activity in mutant Dravet zebrafish, preliminary patient responses, and an ongoing phase III trial in Dravet syndrome.

unread.title: Clinical and molecular analysis of epilepsy-related genes in patients with Dravet syndrome.
unread.why: The study applies targeted exome sequencing and orthogonal verification to characterize SCN1A and candidate genetic-modifier variants in Dravet syndrome pedigrees.

unread.title: Does long-term phenytoin have a place in Dravet syndrome?
unread.why: The four-patient series provides direct evidence that long-term phenytoin can reduce seizure frequency, duration, and status epilepticus in selected patients with Dravet syndrome.

unread.title: Use of Stiripentol in Dravet Syndrome: A Guide for Clinicians.
unread.why: This review reports clinical-trial and real-world efficacy data for stiripentol, including seizure control and prevention of status epilepticus, in Dravet syndrome.

unread.title: Fenfluramine for treatment-resistant epilepsy in Dravet syndrome and other genetically mediated epilepsies.
unread.why: This review summarizes preclinical animal-model evidence and a randomized controlled trial demonstrating substantial seizure reduction with fenfluramine in Dravet syndrome.

unread.title: Relieving the Weight: Fenfluramine's Re-emergence as Antiseizure Medication for Lennox-Gastaut and Dravet Syndrome.
unread.why: The abstract reports phase 2 and phase 3 efficacy and safety data for fenfluramine in patients with Dravet syndrome or Lennox-Gastaut syndrome.

unread.title: Dravet syndrome diagnosed in adults.
unread.why: This case series reports four adults diagnosed through genetic testing and highlights a diagnostic approach for previously unrecognized Dravet syndrome or SCN1A-related epilepsy.

unread.title: Efficacy of Dravet Syndrome Treatments in a Subset of Individuals with 2q24.3 Deletion: A-5 Patient Case Series.
unread.why: This five-patient case series provides treatment-response data in Dravet syndrome associated with 2q24.3 deletions and identifies effective and ineffective antiseizure medications.

unread.title: Structure-Activity Relationship Study on Soticlestat Derivatives for the Discovery of CYP46A1 (CH24H) Inhibitors.
unread.why: The study designs and experimentally evaluates three potent CYP46A1 inhibitor series intended to improve upon soticlestat for Dravet and Lennox-Gastaut syndromes.

unread.title: Low-dose fenfluramine in the treatment of neurologic disorders: experience in Dravet syndrome.
unread.why: The paper reports clinical observations and prospective-study results indicating seizure reduction and tolerability with low-dose fenfluramine in Dravet syndrome.

unread.title: Dravet syndrome.
unread.why: This review summarizes evidence that established antiseizure medications, cannabidiol, and fenfluramine reduce seizures in Dravet syndrome and discusses effects on quality of life and cognition.

unread.title: Individualized treatment approaches: Fenfluramine, a novel antiepileptic medication for the treatment of seizures in Dravet syndrome.
unread.why: The paper traces fenfluramine from clinical observations through zebrafish preclinical testing to a successful phase 3 trial for Dravet syndrome.

unread.title: Current Treatment Strategies and Future Treatment Options for Dravet Syndrome.
unread.why: This disease-specific review identifies established seizure treatments and management strategies, including avoidance of sodium-channel blockers and multidisciplinary status-epilepticus planning, while summarizing emerging targeted approaches.

unread.title: Adults with a history of possible Dravet syndrome: an illustration of the importance of analysis of the SCN1A gene.
unread.why: The study provides direct evidence that SCN1A testing can diagnose children with Dravet syndrome and detect parental somatic mosaicism associated with a mild adult phenotype and high offspring recurrence risk.

unread.title: Stiripentol : in severe myoclonic epilepsy of infancy (dravet syndrome).
unread.why: The review reports randomized-trial efficacy showing that adjunctive stiripentol substantially reduces seizures in Dravet syndrome, with a defined responder outcome and additional long-term evidence.

unread.title: Stiripentol for the treatment of seizures in Dravet syndrome.
unread.why: The review summarizes clinical evidence and regulatory status of stiripentol and other antiseizure treatments for Dravet syndrome, including reduced seizures and status-epilepticus burden.

unread.title: Perampanel Reduces Hyperthermia-Induced Seizures in Dravet Syndrome Mouse Model.
unread.why: Direct experiments in a Dravet syndrome mouse model show that perampanel suppresses spontaneous and heat-induced seizures and has synergistic effects with stiripentol or valproate.

unread.title: AAV delivery of RNA editing machinery rescues SUDEP and seizure phenotype in a mouse model of Dravet Syndrome
unread.why: The study demonstrates proof-of-concept AAV-mediated RNA editing that increases endogenous Scn1a expression and reduces SUDEP, febrile seizures, and seizure duration in a Dravet syndrome mouse model.

unread.title: Disrupted inhibitory interneuron development in SCN1A Dravet syndrome revealed by patient-derived subpallial organoids.
unread.why: The paper establishes a patient-derived human organoid platform, identifies early interneuron abnormalities, and shows partial restoration of neuronal activity by the approved Dravet drug fenfluramine.

unread.title: PV interneuron-targeted CRISPRa rescue of SCN1A haploinsufficiency in Dravet syndrome
unread.why: Direct preclinical data show that PV-selective AAV CRISPR activation restores SCN1A expression and improves survival and heat-induced seizures in Dravet models while showing CNS delivery in macaques.

unread.title: Developmental dysregulation of chandelier cell excitability in a mouse model of Dravet Syndrome
unread.why: The study provides a reusable cell-type-specific mouse-model and measurement approach that identifies persistent chandelier-cell excitability deficits relevant to Dravet pathogenesis.

unread.title: Reduction of Nav1.1 in the dorsal striatum preferentially increases hyperthermia-induced generalized seizures compared with the neocortex and nucleus accumbens
unread.why: The region-specific conditional knockout experiments identify dorsal striatum as unusually vulnerable to partial Nav1.1 loss and provide a circuit-level experimental method for studying Dravet seizure susceptibility.

unread.title: Long-lasting astrocyte remodeling in Dravet Syndrome Scn1a +/– mouse model
unread.why: The study provides a longitudinal Dravet mouse model and shows persistent hippocampal and cortical GFAP abnormalities that can serve as astrocyte-remodeling biomarkers alongside seizure and behavioral endpoints.

unread.title: Reversible Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension Due to Fenfluramine in a Young Child: A Case Report.
unread.why: The pediatric case demonstrates that fenfluramine can markedly reduce seizures in an SCN1B-related developmental epileptic encephalopathy while establishing serial echocardiography as a safety-monitoring solution for pulmonary arterial hypertension.

unread.title: Dravet syndrome: diverse seizure phenotypes with various triggers and developmental outcome- A case series from a LMIC.
unread.why: This Dravet syndrome case series provides disease-specific treatment-response data for several antiseizure medications and documents seizure and developmental outcomes.

unread.title: Cenobamate in pediatric Dravet syndrome: two responder cases highlighting the limits of simple "sodium-channel blocker" labeling.
unread.why: Two pediatric SCN1A-associated Dravet syndrome cases report substantial seizure reduction or suppression with adjunctive cenobamate, including evidence that withdrawal worsened seizures.

unread.title: Fenfluramine Attenuates Retinal Microglial Activation but Does Not Rescue Structural and Vascular Deficits in a Rat Model of Dravet Syndrome.
unread.why: The study directly tests fenfluramine in a Dravet syndrome rat model and identifies multimodal retinal measures as potential noninvasive biomarkers of disease progression and treatment response.

unread.title: Efficacy and safety of fenfluramine in Dravet syndrome: The impact of patient clinical characteristics.
unread.why: Pooled randomized-trial data in 348 Dravet syndrome patients show fenfluramine-associated seizure and global-functioning benefits across age, treatment-history, and SCN1A subgroups with a reassuring safety profile.

unread.title: Clobazam and Valproate, but Lamotrigine, a Sodium Channel Inhibitor, Reduce the Incidence of Hyperthermia-Induced Clonic Seizures in Dravet Syndrome Mice: Assessment of Anti-Seizure Effects in Mice Using a Stabilized Ambient Temperature System.
unread.why: The authors validate a mouse hyperthermia-induced seizure assay and show that clobazam and valproate reduce seizures in a Dravet syndrome model, providing a reusable preclinical testing system.

unread.title: Scn1b deletion in adult mice results in seizures and SUDEP.
unread.why: The study develops an adult-onset Scn1b deletion model that reproduces Dravet-associated seizures and SUDEP and tests whether developmental defects are necessary for epileptogenesis.

unread.title: 4-Phenylbutyrate promoted wild-type γ-aminobutyric acid type A receptor trafficking, reduced endoplasmic reticulum stress, and mitigated seizures in Gabrg2<sup>+/Q390X</sup> mice associated with Dravet syndrome.
unread.why: 4-phenylbutyrate is directly tested in a Dravet-associated GABRG2 model and reduces receptor aggregation, ER stress, seizures, and EEG abnormalities.

unread.title: Epilepsy and sudden unexpected death in epilepsy in a mouse model of human SCN1B-linked developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
unread.why: The paper creates and validates a patient-variant SCN1B mouse model with Dravet-overlapping fever-sensitive seizures, EEG discharges, myoclonus, and premature mortality.

unread.title: The therapeutic effect of stiripentol in Gabrg2<sup>+/Q390X</sup> mice associated with epileptic encephalopathy.
unread.why: The study directly tests stiripentol monotherapy and stiripentol-diazepam combination therapy in a GABRG2-associated Dravet mouse model and identifies an effective add-on regimen.

unread.title: Neonatal but not juvenile gene therapy reduces seizures and prolongs lifespan in SCN1B-Dravet syndrome mice.
unread.why: AAV-mediated SCN1B replacement in neonatal Scn1b-null mice restores cortical excitability, reduces seizures, prevents hyperthermia-induced seizures, and prolongs survival.

unread.title: "Virtual patch clamp analysis" for predicting the functional significance of pathogenic variants in sodium channels.
unread.why: The paper validates a molecular-dynamics and structural-modeling method on SCN1A variants from Dravet patients and shows agreement with functional patch-clamp results.

unread.title: [Genotype and phenotype of female Dravet syndrome with PCDH19 mutations].
unread.why: The study identifies PCDH19 mutations in female Dravet syndrome patients and supports routine genetic screening when SCN1A testing is negative.

unread.title: Trial of Cannabidiol for Drug-Resistant Seizures in the Dravet Syndrome.
unread.why: A randomized controlled trial provides direct clinical evidence that adjunctive cannabidiol reduces convulsive seizures in Dravet syndrome.

unread.title: Fenfluramine hydrochloride for the treatment of seizures in Dravet syndrome: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
unread.why: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial directly shows that fenfluramine substantially reduces convulsive seizure frequency in Dravet syndrome.

unread.title: Optimizing the Diagnosis and Management of Dravet Syndrome: Recommendations From a North American Consensus Panel.
unread.why: This consensus statement provides actionable diagnostic, treatment, seizure-management, and comorbidity-monitoring recommendations specifically for Dravet syndrome.

unread.title: Incidence of Dravet Syndrome in a US Population.
unread.why: The population study defines practical clinical identification criteria and supports early SCN1A genetic testing in infants with prolonged febrile seizures.

unread.title: Clemizole and modulators of serotonin signalling suppress seizures in Dravet syndrome.
unread.why: The study combines a Dravet-relevant zebrafish drug-screening platform with experimental validation of clemizole and serotonin-modulating drugs, including limited clinical use in Dravet patients.

unread.title: The voltage-gated sodium channel Scn8a is a genetic modifier of severe myoclonic epilepsy of infancy.
unread.why: The study experimentally demonstrates that Scn8a modification reduces seizure susceptibility and rescues lethality in a Dravet/SMEI mouse model.

unread.title: The SCN1A mutation database: updating information and analysis of the relationships among genotype, functional alteration, and phenotype.
unread.why: The paper establishes a curated SCN1A mutation database and demonstrates how functional alteration data can support pathogenicity assessment and patient management.

unread.title: A Transient Developmental Window of Fast-Spiking Interneuron Dysfunction in a Mouse Model of Dravet Syndrome.
unread.why: The study directly characterizes a Dravet syndrome mouse model and provides electrophysiological and immunohistochemical assays for a central disease mechanism.

unread.title: Quality of life and comorbidities associated with Dravet syndrome severity: a multinational cohort survey.
unread.why: The large Dravet cohort establishes measurable relationships among seizure burden, comorbidities, quality of life, and health-service use.

unread.title: Clinical and genetic factors predicting Dravet syndrome in infants with SCN1A mutations.
unread.why: The study identifies clinical and mutational predictors that distinguish Dravet syndrome from milder outcomes and provides diagnostic performance estimates.

unread.title: Progressive gait deterioration in adolescents with Dravet syndrome.
unread.why: The study establishes gait deterioration measures and mobility outcomes for Dravet syndrome using standardized clinical and radiographic assessments.

unread.title: Cacna1g is a genetic modifier of epilepsy in a mouse model of Dravet syndrome.
unread.why: The paper provides direct evidence in a Dravet mouse model that reducing Cacna1g expression improves survival and spontaneous seizures, identifying a genetically testable therapeutic strategy.

unread.title: Antisense oligonucleotides restore excitability, GABA signalling and sodium current density in a Dravet syndrome model.
unread.why: The study directly tests an SCN1A antisense treatment in a Dravet mouse model and restores sodium current, interneuron excitability, GABA signaling, and seizure-related electrophysiological abnormalities.

unread.title: Discovery of Soticlestat, a Potent and Selective Inhibitor for Cholesterol 24-Hydroxylase (CH24H).
unread.why: The study develops and characterizes soticlestat, a brain-penetrant CYP46A1 inhibitor that reduces brain 24-hydroxycholesterol and is being clinically investigated for Dravet syndrome.

unread.title: Audit of use of stiripentol in adults with Dravet syndrome.
unread.why: This clinical audit provides direct real-world evidence for stiripentol efficacy, seizure response, adverse effects, and retention in adults with Dravet syndrome.

unread.title: Efficacy and tolerability of add-on stiripentol in real-world clinical practice: An observational study in Dravet syndrome and non-Dravet developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
unread.why: This observational study reports real-world efficacy, seizure outcomes, and tolerability of adjunctive stiripentol specifically in children and adults with Dravet syndrome.

unread.title: Combined Antiseizure Efficacy of Cannabidiol and Clonazepam in a Conditional Mouse Model of Dravet Syndrome.
unread.why: The study directly tests clonazepam and cannabidiol combination treatment in a conditional mouse model of Dravet syndrome and reports reduced seizure duration and increased seizure threshold.

unread.title: Testing of putative antiseizure medications in a preclinical Dravet syndrome zebrafish model.
unread.why: This study evaluates a Dravet syndrome zebrafish platform and two seizure assays for screening antiseizure candidates, while identifying drugs with positive or negative preclinical results.

unread.title: Fenfluramine treatment in pediatric patients with Dravet syndrome reduces seizure burden and overall healthcare costs: A retrospective and observational real-world study.
unread.why: This real-world pediatric Dravet study reports fenfluramine treatment outcomes, seizure reductions, medication use, and healthcare utilization in patients with pathogenic SCN1A variants.

unread.title: Genetic Diagnosis of Dravet Syndrome Using Next Generation Sequencing-Based Epilepsy Gene Panel Testing.
unread.why: This study demonstrates targeted next-generation sequencing as an efficient diagnostic approach for clinically diagnosed Dravet syndrome and reports SCN1A and PCDH19 findings in patients.
